ai.description: This frog reaches 5–8 cm. It features a golden-brown back, white belly, and a distinct dark stripe from the snout through the eye. Long, slender limbs and prominent dorsolateral folds are diagnostic.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable cue for *Hylarana indica* is the presence of a distinct, continuous white or cream-colored dorsolateral fold that contrasts sharply against its dark flanks.
ai.habitat: *Hylarana indica* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found near streams at mid-to-high elevations between 600 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Indian Golden-backed Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects along the banks of streams and forest pools.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hylarana indica* breeds during the monsoon season, laying large clutches of eggs in stagnant or slow-moving water bodies. The larvae undergo typical aquatic development.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hylarana indica* is found in the Western Ghats of India, spanning states like Kerala, Karnataka, and Maharashtra at elevations between 200 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Indian Golden-backed Frog produces a series of rapid, high-pitched "tink-tink" chirps, typically heard near forest streams and rocky pools during the monsoon.
